Getting Started with tidycreel.connect

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Overview

tidycreel.connect provides a unified connection layer for the tidycreel creel survey package. It lets you load interview, count, catch, and length data from three backends:

Backend When to use Status
CSV Flat files from a data export or field laptop Loads data
REST API A service returning JSON, described by a profile you supply Loads data
Database (DBI) An agency production database — SQL Server via ODBC, or any DBI driver Loads data

Every creel_connection is accepted by every fetch_*() function and passes cleanly into tidycreel::add_interviews(). A database connection reads each table by the name the schema gives it, then puts the rows through the same rename, coercion and validation as the other backends, so which backend the frame came from does not change what comes out.

list_creels() and search_creels() are the exception: discovery asks a source which surveys it holds, and a database connection addresses one set of tables rather than a catalogue. They abort on a database connection, saying that, and are available on the API backend where the service defines them.

Connections are read-only

No backend writes anything. The CSV backend only reads the files named in the schema; the API backend issues GET requests only; a database connection only ever reads the tables the schema names. No table is created, altered, dropped or written to, no row is inserted or updated, and no file is written — including the files a CSV connection reads. Pointing a connection at a production database or an agency’s live export cannot modify it.

Installation prerequisites 

# Core package (already installed if you have tidycreel)
install.packages("tidycreel.connect")

# Required for YAML-based connections
install.packages("config")

# Required for SQL Server connections
install.packages("odbc")

You also need a native ODBC driver on your OS — see the README for platform-specific install instructions.

1. Define a column-mapping schema

A creel_schema tells tidycreel.connect which columns in your data files correspond to the canonical names used by tidycreel. Create one with tidycreel::creel_schema():

library(tidycreel)
library(tidycreel.connect)

schema <- creel_schema(
  survey_type       = "instantaneous",
  # Table names: required by the database backend, ignored for CSV.
  # harvest_lengths_table / release_lengths_table both fall back to
  # lengths_table, so a source keeping one lengths table needs only this.
  interviews_table  = "vwInterviews",
  counts_table      = "vwCounts",
  catch_table       = "vwCatch",
  lengths_table     = "vwLengths",
  # Column mappings: right-hand side is the name in your data source
  interview_uid_col = "InterviewID",
  date_col          = "SurveyDate",
  effort_col        = "EffortHours",
  catch_col         = "TotalCatch",
  trip_status_col   = "TripStatus",
  bank_anglers_col  = "BankAnglers",
  # Party size: map it whenever your source records it. Unmapped, the interview
  # effort is party-hours and every rate denominator is off by the mean party
  # size. Bus-route designs additionally need site_col and circuit_col.
  n_anglers_col     = "NumberAnglers",
  angler_type_col   = "AnglerType",
  catch_uid_col     = "CatchUID",
  species_col       = "SpeciesCode",
  catch_count_col   = "CatchCount",
  catch_type_col    = "CatchCategory",
  length_uid_col    = "LengthUID",
  length_mm_col     = "LengthMM",
  length_type_col   = "LengthType"
)

schema
#> <creel_schema: instantaneous>
#> 
#> ── interviews: vwInterviews ──
#> 
#> date -> SurveyDate
#> catch -> TotalCatch
#> effort -> EffortHours
#> trip_status -> TripStatus
#> n_anglers -> NumberAnglers
#> angler_type -> AnglerType
#> interview_uid -> InterviewID
#> 
#> ── counts: vwCounts ──
#> 
#> bank_anglers -> BankAnglers
#> 
#> ── catch: vwCatch ──
#> 
#> catch_uid -> CatchUID
#> species -> SpeciesCode
#> catch_count -> CatchCount
#> catch_type -> CatchCategory
#> 
#> ── lengths: vwLengths ──
#> 
#> length_uid -> LengthUID
#> length_mm -> LengthMM
#> length_type -> LengthType

2a. Connect using a YAML config file (recommended)

YAML config keeps connection details out of your scripts. Create a file creel-config.yml:

# creel-config.yml — CSV backend example
default:
  backend: csv
  files:
    interviews:      data/interviews.csv
    counts:          data/counts.csv
    catch:           data/catch.csv
    harvest_lengths: data/harvest_lengths.csv
    release_lengths: data/release_lengths.csv
  schema:
    survey_type: instantaneous

Then connect:

conn <- creel_connect_from_yaml("creel-config.yml")

SQL Server YAML config

Credentials must never be stored as plain text. Use the config package’s !expr tag to inject them from environment variables:

# creel-config.yml — SQL Server backend example
default:
  backend:   sqlserver
  server:    myserver.example.com
  database:  CreelDB
  auth_type: password
  username:  !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_USER")
  password:  !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_PASS")
  # Optional. These are the defaults: Driver 18, encrypted, certificate
  # verified. Turning either protection off warns on every connect.
  # driver: ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server
  # encrypt: true
  # trust_server_certificate: false
  schema:
    survey_type:       instantaneous
    interviews_table:  vwInterviews
    counts_table:      vwCounts
    catch_table:       vwCatch
    lengths_table:     vwLengths
    interview_uid_col: InterviewID
    date_col:          SurveyDate
    effort_col:        EffortHours
    catch_col:         TotalCatch
    trip_status_col:   TripStatus
    count_col:         AnglerCount
    catch_uid_col:     CatchUID
    species_col:       SpeciesCode
    catch_count_col:   CatchCount
    catch_type_col:    CatchCategory
    length_uid_col:    LengthUID
    length_mm_col:     LengthMM
    length_type_col:   LengthType

Set credentials before connecting:

Sys.setenv(CREEL_USER = "your_username", CREEL_PASS = "your_password")
conn <- creel_connect_from_yaml("creel-config.yml")

For Windows integrated authentication (Windows only):

auth_type: windows

Note: auth_type: windows aborts immediately on macOS and Linux with a helpful error message directing you to use auth_type: password instead.

Multiple environments

The config environment block lets you switch between development and production databases without editing the file:

default:
  backend: csv
  files:
    interviews: data/dev/interviews.csv
    # ...

production:
  backend:   sqlserver
  server:    prod.example.com
  database:  CreelDB
  auth_type: password
  username:  !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_USER")
  password:  !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_PASS")
  # ...
# Default (CSV for development)
conn_dev <- creel_connect_from_yaml("creel-config.yml")

# Production SQL Server
conn_prod <- creel_connect_from_yaml("creel-config.yml", config = "production")

REST API profile

tidycreel.connect ships no endpoint paths and no JSON field names for any API. Those describe one deployment, and a built-in default would decode that service’s payload while silently misreading everyone else’s — so endpoints, api_field_map and uid_param are all required, and the connection aborts without them.

Keep them in a profile rather than in your analysis code. A commented template with invented names is installed with the package:

file.edit(
  system.file("extdata", "api-profile-example.yml", package = "tidycreel.connect")
)
# my-api.yml — API backend example
default:
  backend: api
  base_url: "https://api.example.org/creel/"
  uid_param: "survey_id"
  creel_uids: ["survey-2016-001"]
  schema:
    survey_type: instantaneous
  endpoints:
    interviews: "v2/interviews"
    counts: "v2/counts"
  field_map:
    interviews:
      interview_uid: "InterviewID"
      date: "SurveyDate"
      trip_status: "TripStatus"
      effort_hours: "HoursFished"
      n_anglers: "PartySize"     # map it: see section 4
    counts:
      date: "SurveyDate"
      bank_anglers: "ShoreAnglers"
conn <- creel_connect_from_yaml("~/.config/tidycreel/my-api.yml")

Pointing the same script at a different file is how it runs against a different organisation’s API.

2b. Connect programmatically

You can also construct a connection directly without a YAML file.

CSV backend 

# Build small toy CSV files for this example
tmp_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()

interviews_csv <- file.path(tmp_dir, "interviews.csv")
counts_csv <- file.path(tmp_dir, "counts.csv")
catch_csv <- file.path(tmp_dir, "catch.csv")
lengths_csv <- file.path(tmp_dir, "lengths.csv")

readr::write_csv(
  data.frame(
    InterviewID  = 1:4,
    SurveyDate   = "2024-06-01",
    EffortHours  = c(2.0, 3.5, 1.5, 4.0),
    TotalCatch   = c(5L, 8L, 2L, 6L),
    TripStatus   = "complete"
  ),
  interviews_csv
)
readr::write_csv(
  data.frame(SurveyDate = "2024-06-01", BankAnglers = 12L),
  counts_csv
)
readr::write_csv(
  data.frame(
    CatchUID    = 1:3,
    InterviewID = c(1L, 1L, 2L),
    SpeciesCode = c("WAE", "WAE", "LMB"),
    CatchCount  = c(2L, 1L, 3L),
    CatchCategory   = "harvest"
  ),
  catch_csv
)
readr::write_csv(
  data.frame(
    LengthUID   = 1:2,
    InterviewID = c(1L, 2L),
    SpeciesCode = c("WAE", "LMB"),
    LengthMM    = c(420L, 380L),
    LengthType  = c("harvest", "harvest")
  ),
  lengths_csv
)

# Connect with a named list of file paths
conn <- creel_connect(
  con = list(
    interviews      = interviews_csv,
    counts          = counts_csv,
    catch           = catch_csv,
    harvest_lengths = lengths_csv,
    release_lengths = lengths_csv
  ),
  schema = schema
)

conn
#> <creel_connection: csv>
#> Status: ready
#> Backend: CSV
#> interviews → /tmp/RtmpN5NKRm/file1ce47deb3dca/interviews.csv
#> counts → /tmp/RtmpN5NKRm/file1ce47deb3dca/counts.csv
#> catch → /tmp/RtmpN5NKRm/file1ce47deb3dca/catch.csv
#> harvest_lengths → /tmp/RtmpN5NKRm/file1ce47deb3dca/lengths.csv
#> release_lengths → /tmp/RtmpN5NKRm/file1ce47deb3dca/lengths.csv
#> Schema: <creel_schema: instantaneous>
#> 
#> ── interviews: vwInterviews ──
#> 
#> date -> SurveyDate
#> catch -> TotalCatch
#> effort -> EffortHours
#> trip_status -> TripStatus
#> n_anglers -> NumberAnglers
#> angler_type -> AnglerType
#> interview_uid -> InterviewID
#> 
#> ── counts: vwCounts ──
#> 
#> bank_anglers -> BankAnglers
#> 
#> ── catch: vwCatch ──
#> 
#> catch_uid -> CatchUID
#> species -> SpeciesCode
#> catch_count -> CatchCount
#> catch_type -> CatchCategory
#> 
#> ── lengths: vwLengths ──
#> 
#> length_uid -> LengthUID
#> length_mm -> LengthMM
#> length_type -> LengthType

SQL Server / DBI backend 

library(DBI)
library(odbc)

dbi_con <- dbConnect(
  odbc(),
  driver   = "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
  server   = "myserver.example.com",
  database = "CreelDB",
  uid      = Sys.getenv("CREEL_USER"),
  pwd      = Sys.getenv("CREEL_PASS"),
  encrypt  = "yes"  # Driver 18's default; Driver 17 needs it said
)

conn <- creel_connect(dbi_con, schema, auth_type = "password")

3. Fetch data

Once you have a creel_connection, use the fetch_*() family to load each table. All functions return a tibble with canonical column names defined by the schema.

interviews <- fetch_interviews(conn)
counts <- fetch_counts(conn)
catch_data <- fetch_catch(conn)
harvest_lengths <- fetch_harvest_lengths(conn)
release_lengths <- fetch_release_lengths(conn)

# Date columns are coerced to R Date regardless of backend
class(interviews$date)
#> [1] "Date"

# Species codes are coerced to character (SQL Server may store as integer)
class(catch_data$species)
#> [1] "character"

interviews
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   interview_uid date       catch_count effort trip_status
#>   <chr>         <date>           <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>      
#> 1 1             2024-06-01           5    2   complete   
#> 2 2             2024-06-01           8    3.5 complete   
#> 3 3             2024-06-01           2    1.5 complete   
#> 4 4             2024-06-01           6    4   complete

4. Integrate with tidycreel

The fetched tibbles slot directly into the tidycreel estimation workflow. fetch_interviews() returns a tibble with canonical column names — pass it to tidycreel::add_interviews() along with a creel_design object:

# First, build a creel_design from your calendar and count data
# (see the tidycreel getting-started vignette for the full workflow)
design <- creel_design(
  calendar    = my_calendar,
  date        = date,
  strata      = stratum,
  design_type = "instantaneous"
)

# Then attach the fetched interview data. Pass n_anglers when the schema maps a
# party-size column: without it add_interviews() assumes one angler per
# interview and warns, and the effort it carries is party-hours rather than
# angler-hours.
design <- add_interviews(
  design,
  interviews  = interviews,
  catch       = catch_count,
  effort      = effort,
  trip_status = trip_status,
  n_anglers   = n_anglers
)

# Now estimate
estimate_effort(design)
estimate_catch_rate(design, species = "WAE")

The column names (catch_count, effort, trip_status) come from the creel_schema column mappings defined earlier — they are the canonical names that fetch_interviews() renames to, regardless of what your source database calls them.

See vignette("getting-started", package = "tidycreel") for a complete end-to-end estimation walkthrough.

Credential security

Never store credentials as plain text in scripts or YAML files. The recommended approach:

  1. Store in .Renviron (user-level, never committed):

    CREEL_USER=your_username
CREEL_PASS=your_password

  2. Reference via !expr in YAML:

    username: !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_USER")
password: !expr Sys.getenv("CREEL_PASS")

  3. Reload without restarting R after editing .Renviron:

    readRenviron("~/.Renviron")

Tip: Add .Renviron to your global .gitignore to prevent accidental credential commits.
